title: Hutchinson expands utility assistance program to residents of all ages - Hutch Post
text:
Hutchinson expands utility assistance program to residents of all ages 📱 The new Hutch Post app is here.
 Download now Oct 28, 2026 Hutchinson expands utility assistance program to residents of all ages
 Posted Oct 28, 2026 10:15 AM 
 HUTCHINSON, Kan. — The City of Hutchinson is accepting applications for its 2027 Low-Income Water and Sewer Assistance Program, which has been expanded to include eligible residents of all ages.
 Beginning in 2027, the program will no longer require applicants to be 65 or older. The change allows qualifying low-income households to receive assistance with their monthly water and sewer bills regardless of age.
 The program provides credits toward the base monthly water and sewer fees for approved applicants, helping reduce utility expenses for eligible households.
 To qualify, applicants must have residential water or sewer service in their name and meet income requirements based on the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program, or LIHEAP, guidelines. Household income cannot exceed 150% of the federal poverty level.
 The assistance is limited to residential utility customers and is not available for business use or landowners who do not meet the residential service requirements.
 City officials said applications will be processed on a first-come, first-served basis until the available funding has been allocated. The Hutchinson City Council has budgeted funds for the program in both 2026 and 2027.
 Residents who have already qualified for LIHEAP may use their acceptance letter to simplify the application process.
 Applications must be submitted annually, including by residents who received assistance in previous years.
 Residents can apply online through the city's 2027 utility assistance application . Paper applications are also available at the Utility Billing office at Hutchinson City Hall.
 Applicants will receive a confirmation email once their application has been processed.
